body:
## The problem in plain terms

A developer can use one ADP login with Claude Code and Codex, but Claude Desktop needs separate manual settings and ADP's Anthropic Messages path loses tool fields. Desktop users need the same governed gateway connection and a complete client-tool exchange. Bedrock's published examples show the protocol, but this deployment's account, role, region and model still need live validation.

**The fix in one line:** Prove Bedrock support in cloud, then deliver gateway tool fidelity, Desktop setup and a repeatable cloud acceptance test.

## Description

Support Claude Desktop's Gateway provider with the existing ADP login, model policy, metering and Bedrock backend. Scope the promise to capabilities proven for the selected Bedrock model. This issue is the delivery index; developer runs belong on the children.

**Hard gate:** #6851 must record a GO result for the core direct-Bedrock tool loop and streaming under the target cloud identity before product source changes or implementation dispatch. A NO-GO blocks or narrows dependent work.

## Impact analysis

- **Who benefits:** Desktop Chat/Code/Cowork users relying on client tools.
- **Who's impacted:** gateway protocol, model policy, usage accounting, CLI onboarding and cloud tests.
- **Cost / quota:** bounded Bedrock probes and smoke invokes; no planned persistent AWS resources or database migration.

| Bug class | Blast radius |
|---|---|
| Tool request/result lost | Desktop cannot finish a tool task. |
| Unsupported feature forwarded | Model rejects a session mid-turn. |
| Wrong identity/deployment | Usage is misattributed or routed incorrectly. |
| Stream/auth failure | Tool action can fail or be retried ambiguously. |

## Design

| Order | Native child | Work | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #6851 | Cloud Bedrock InvokeModel, streaming and CountTokens proof; capability matrix | — |
| 2 | #6852 | Preserve supported tool definitions, choices, results, JSON Schema and beta fields | #6851; coordinate existing #790 |
| 3 | #6853 | Preserve non-stream/SSE tool events, stop reasons, usage and errors | #6851, #6852 |
| 4 | #6854 | Entitlement-safe Claude models and validated token counting | #6851, #6852 |
| 5 | #6855 | Deployment-pinned adp claude-desktop setup and refresh-safe helper | #6851, #6854 |
| 6 | #6856 | Clean cloud end-to-end suite and runbook | #6851–#6855 |

#790 already owns the basic stripped-tools bug for another epic. Coordinate a single implementation/PR; this epic closes only when that defect is resolved and the broader Desktop contract passes. Desktop executes client tools; ADP transports tool calls/results and invokes Bedrock. Unsupported model features must produce explicit limits rather than silent field loss.

AWS contracts: [Claude Messages](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-anthropic-claude-messages-request-response.html), [tool use](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-anthropic-claude-messages-tool-use.html), [CountTokens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_CountTokens.html).

## Deployment

The epic itself deploys nothing. Gateway children use gateway-deploy.yml in dev; CLI rollout and cloud workflow follow their child instructions. Promote to production only after its own account/model cloud run passes. Revert the relevant child PR if smoke fails.

## Validation

- **Before code:** #6851 publishes redacted direct-Bedrock evidence with account, role, region, model, exact event shapes and GO/NO-GO per feature.
- **At PR:** children run schema, tool-round-trip, streaming, policy and CLI regression tests.
- **Post-merge:** #6856 runs a Desktop-shaped two-turn tool task from a clean cloud pod through the deployed gateway with a real scoped token, checks refresh and usage attribution, and links the passing workflow run here.
- **Acceptance:** all children and #790 are resolved, the target environment's cloud suite passes, and a manual Desktop smoke confirms the settings experience.

## Non-goals

Do not promise every Desktop beta, server-hosted tool or Bedrock model. Do not change existing Claude Code or Codex configuration during Desktop setup.
title: Claude Desktop Support via ADP

body:
## The problem in plain terms

Claude Desktop can ask a model to use a tool, but a published API example does not prove that this ADP account, model, region, and cloud agent role can complete that exchange. Building a gateway adapter first could produce code that the deployed Bedrock model rejects. The team needs a small live proof before modifying product code.

**The fix in one line:** Run bounded direct Bedrock tool-loop probes in cloud and publish a GO/NO-GO compatibility matrix.

## Description

Prove the Bedrock Runtime calls that Claude Desktop support will depend on, from a cloud execution identity matching the intended deployment. This story is the hard prerequisite for all product implementation children of #6850.

The output is a short evidence note with sanitized request and response fixtures, selected model IDs, IAM role/account/region, supported features, exact limits, and a recommendation. Probe execution comes before any ADP product source edit.

## Impact analysis

- **Who benefits:** all implementers and reviewers of #6850; operators get a reproducible basis for enabling Desktop.
- **Who's impacted:** a dev Bedrock model quota and a temporary cloud job/pod only.
- **Cost / quota footprint:** cap each output at 256 tokens, at most two candidate models and a small fixed invocation count; record actual token use/cost estimate.

| Bug class | Blast radius |
|---|---|
| Wrong account, region, model, or role | False GO; later code fails only in deployment. |
| Prompt-only proof without tool result | Fails to establish the required tool round trip. |
| Credential/prompt logged | Leaks a scoped token or test content into CI logs. |
| Optional feature assumed universal | Unsupported model rejects Desktop requests after rollout. |

## Design

Run from a short-lived cloud pod or ARC job with the intended IAM role. First print aws sts get-caller-identity and assert its account equals the deployment target; record region and an entitlement-allowed Claude inference profile. Use boto3 Bedrock Runtime, because AWS CLI does not support streaming operations. No local SSO credentials.

For each selected model, exercise direct InvokeModel with anthropic_version=bedrock-2023-05-31 and:
1. A minimal user message with a custom tool containing nested JSON Schema and tool_choice auto. Verify a tool_use block and stop_reason tool_use. If the model supports forced tool choice, probe that separately; a documented unsupported result is a capability limit, not a reason to fake support.
2. A second call containing the assistant tool_use and user tool_result; verify the final answer uses the result.
3. InvokeModelWithResponseStream for the same shape; record event types, tool input deltas, stop reason, usage, and any error event.
4. CountTokens with input.invokeModel for the same body, if supported and authorized. Distinguish unsupported model/API from missing bedrock:CountTokens permission.
5. A bounded matrix for Desktop-relevant beta/cache/thinking and image/document blocks that later stories intend to support. Mark unsupported items explicitly; do not infer availability from a different model.

Put a redacted probe transcript and fixture JSON in docs/research or an issue attachment/comment. Strip prompts, credentials, account-private headers and model output content where unnecessary. Reference AWS [tool use](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-anthropic-claude-messages-tool-use.html), [request schema](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-anthropic-claude-messages-request-response.html), [streaming API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_InvokeModelWithResponseStream.html), and [CountTokens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_CountTokens.html).

No database/API changes. Reuse the deployment's expected account, gateway model allowlist and existing cloud identity. Core tool loop and streaming must be GO before stories 2-6 change product code.

## Deployment

Probe-only and evidence-note work; no gateway, CLI, Terraform, or agent image deployment. Run against dev; rerun for a different target account/region/model before promoting that target. Remove the temporary pod/job and local fixtures containing sensitive data.

## Validation

- **At-PR/review:** reviewer can reproduce the exact boto3 calls and sees account, role, region, model ID, sanitized event sequence, token use, GO/NO-GO for each feature.
- **Cloud smoke:** one direct two-turn tool exchange plus one streamed exchange succeeds using the stated role; CountTokens result or precise unsupported reason is captured.
- **Regression:** no product files changed, no persistent AWS resource left, no credential in logs.
- **Gate:** if the core tool loop or streaming is NO-GO, stop dependent implementation and update #6850 with the narrowed scope or blocker.
title: Spike: validate Claude Desktop tool protocol against Bedrock from cloud

body:
## The problem in plain terms

Claude Desktop sends tool definitions and later sends tool results, but ADP currently drops important request fields before Bedrock sees them. The model may answer without offering the tool, and complex tool schemas can lose meaning silently.

**The fix in one line:** Preserve only Bedrock-proven Anthropic Messages fields through gateway validation, translation, and invocation.

## Description

Make the ADP Anthropic Messages route carry a Desktop client-tool request and follow-up tool result without loss, while retaining tenant/model policy and explicit errors for unsupported features. Implement only the feature set marked GO by the Bedrock proof child of #6850.

Existing #790 already tracks the basic tools/tool_choice loss for another epic. Coordinate ownership before coding: land or incorporate #790 once, link its PR, and avoid parallel duplicate edits.

## Impact analysis

- **Who benefits:** Desktop Chat/Code/Cowork users relying on client tools; hosted agent gateway callers sharing this route.
- **Who's impacted:** request validation, Bedrock invocation, prompt caching and usage accounting, tenant model policy.
- **Cost / quota footprint:** no new infrastructure; preserved tool definitions increase real input tokens, which must be metered as returned by Bedrock.

| Bug class | Blast radius |
|---|---|
| Tool definitions or JSON Schema fields dropped | Wrong or missing tool calls, especially for nested inputs. |
| Unsupported beta forwarded blindly | Model returns 400 mid-session. |
| Model/policy bypass through raw pass-through | Cross-tenant or disallowed model invocation. |
| Cache control stripped | Unexpected token spend on long tool sessions. |

## Design

Depends on the GO matrix from story 1. On current main inspect modules/gateway/src/proxy/schemas.py, format_translator.py, service.py, and routes.py. The typed AnthropicToolInput currently retains only type/properties/required; AnthropicMessagesRequest accepts tools/tool_choice, but FormatTranslator.anthropic_to_bedrock omits both. Content block models also need a deliberate supported-field contract.

Preserve the validated fields: custom tool definitions including full supported JSON Schema, tool_choice where selected model permits it, assistant tool_use, user tool_result including is_error and supported content, cache_control, and required anthropic_beta body values. Translate the client header version to Bedrock's required anthropic_version; do not send the gateway-only model or stream fields as Bedrock body keys. Keep the existing model resolution, allowlist, auth, budget, and usage path. Return a clear 4xx with feature/model detail for a known unsupported shape; never silently drop a requested tool or beta. Avoid blanket extra=allow on nested content until cloud proof shows Bedrock accepts it.

No database migration. Document request examples and failure codes in the route tests. Reuse #790's basic fix if it lands first; this story owns the remaining Desktop-compatible fidelity.

## Deployment

Backend change on main triggers gateway-deploy.yml for dev. No Terraform or agent-runtime image rebuild. Production promotion is manual after cloud smoke. Rollback by reverting the gateway PR and disabling Desktop onboarding; existing Claude Code Bedrock path remains available.

## Validation

- **At-PR unit:** round-trip a nested tool schema, auto/supported forced tool choice, cache marker, tool_use/tool_result and supported beta through schema to the exact Bedrock body. Assert unsupported fields fail explicitly, not disappear.
- **At-PR integration:** a fake Bedrock client captures the request body and confirms auth/model policy checks still precede invocation; non-tool Claude requests retain behavior.
- **Post-merge cloud:** replay the sanitized direct-Bedrock fixture through the deployed gateway with a scoped user token; compare tool_use and follow-up result with story 1's baseline, plus usage attribution.
- **Regression:** Claude Code Bedrock mode, Codex gateway route, existing Anthropic text requests, and #790 acceptance remain green.
title: Preserve Claude Desktop client-tool requests through the ADP gateway

body:
## The problem in plain terms

A tool call is useful only if Desktop receives the tool name, complete input, stop reason, and a usable stream in the expected order. ADP's stream adapter has not been proven against the chosen Bedrock model's live tool events; a dropped delta or error can leave Desktop waiting or running the wrong action.

**The fix in one line:** Verify and repair Anthropic non-stream and SSE tool response fidelity against cloud-recorded Bedrock events.

## Description

Carry the Bedrock-proven tool response and streaming event sequence through ADP without data loss, including partial tool-input JSON, finish reasons, usage, and provider errors. This story follows the Bedrock proof and request-fidelity story under #6850.

## Impact analysis

- **Who benefits:** Desktop users executing local client tools and any Anthropic Messages gateway client.
- **Who's impacted:** response translation, streaming keepalive, logging/usage, and error handling.
- **Cost / quota footprint:** no new resources; bounded live test invocations. Keepalive traffic stays within existing gateway capacity.

| Bug class | Blast radius |
|---|---|
| input_json_delta reordered or lost | Desktop executes a malformed tool call. |
| Duplicate/missing message_stop | Client hangs or treats a partial result as complete. |
| Bedrock stream error flattened into success | Broken task is reported as a valid answer. |
| Cache/usage fields lost | Accounting and user limits diverge. |

## Design

Depends on story 1 and story 2. Inspect modules/gateway/src/proxy/stream_handler.py, format_translator.py, service.py and routes.py. Preserve the direct Bedrock sequence for message_start, content_block_start, content_block_delta (including input_json_delta), content_block_stop, message_delta with stop_reason tool_use and usage, and message_stop. The gateway may rewrite only the public model ID/response ID needed by the client; it must not mutate tool IDs or streamed JSON fragments. Keep SSE keepalive comments between complete events. Propagate throttling/validation/provider errors in a client-recognizable form and avoid replaying a tool action after a mid-stream failure.

For non-stream responses, preserve all Bedrock-proven content blocks and stop/usage metadata rather than narrowing to text/tool_use if the model returns additional supported blocks. Gate optional thinking/server-tool block types on story 1's matrix. No migration or new auth path.

## Deployment

Gateway backend deploys to dev through gateway-deploy.yml on merge. No Terraform, frontend, or agent image change. Promote manually after cloud replay. Revert this PR if SSE regression appears; the existing Claude Code Bedrock path provides an unaffected fallback.

## Validation

- **At-PR unit:** replay sanitized Bedrock EventStream fixture for a tool call and assert exact SSE event order, tool ID, concatenated input JSON, stop reason and usage; inject throttling/mid-stream exception and assert visible failure.
- **At-PR integration:** run streamed and non-streamed gateway requests with a fake Bedrock client; verify no duplicate terminal event and no hidden tool execution by gateway.
- **Post-merge cloud:** run the streamed two-turn tool loop via the deployed dev gateway from a clean cloud pod, compare with direct baseline, and confirm usage/request ID records.
- **Regression:** plain text SSE, long-thinking keepalive, client cancellation, and existing Bedrock pass-through tests stay green.
title: Relay Claude Desktop tool responses and streams without loss

body:
## The problem in plain terms

Claude Desktop needs a model picker and a token count that match what the ADP user can actually call. ADP currently offers general gateway aliases and estimates tokens from character length, which can hide tool-schema and image costs or present models Desktop cannot use.

**The fix in one line:** Give Desktop an entitlement-safe Claude model set and Bedrock-validated token counting with honest fallback behavior.

## Description

Make model discovery and token counting fit the selected Claude Desktop Gateway path. Use the Bedrock proof from #6850 to decide whether exact CountTokens is supported for the chosen model and role; do not label a character estimate as an exact count.

## Impact analysis

- **Who benefits:** Desktop users choosing an available Claude model and planning long tool sessions.
- **Who's impacted:** gateway model policy, count-tokens route, IAM if a new CountTokens permission is actually required, and CLI-provided model selection.
- **Cost / quota footprint:** CountTokens calls consume API quota; cap repeated calls and document their cost behavior. No database migration planned.

| Bug class | Blast radius |
|---|---|
| Non-Claude/disallowed model offered | Desktop fails after model selection or bypasses intended policy display. |
| Fake exact token count | Context/budget decisions are wrong on tool-heavy requests. |
| CountTokens permission missing | Every Desktop count request fails with 403. |
| Discovery change breaks existing clients | Codex or other gateway callers lose model IDs. |

## Design

Depends on story 1; coordinate with request fidelity story 2 for the Bedrock body used in counting. Current main: modules/gateway/src/proxy/model_resolver.py supplies /v1/models and modules/gateway/src/proxy/routes.py estimates /v1/messages/count_tokens as text length / 4. CountTokens accepts an InvokeModel-shaped body via input.invokeModel when the target model supports it.

Choose a backward-compatible Desktop model strategy: either a Desktop-specific, user-authorized listing/parameter or an explicit model list in the setup artifact. Do not globally remove existing /v1/models entries. Ensure the returned/default model IDs resolve to actual allowed Claude inference profiles for the user's org/team and selected deployment.

For /v1/messages/count_tokens, apply the same schema transformation and model access check as actual inference, then call Bedrock Runtime CountTokens only for model/region/role combinations proven in story 1. Include tools and other supported fields in the body. If CountTokens is unavailable, return an explicit unsupported response or documented Desktop-compatible fallback agreed from the cloud test; never silently claim precision. Surface access failures separately from unsupported models. No migration; reuse existing auth and model resolver.

## Deployment

Gateway backend change triggers gateway-deploy.yml on merge to dev. An IAM permission change, if required by the probe, must be separately reviewed/applied through existing gateway infra workflow; do not broaden agent-worker IAM just to satisfy counting. Production promotion manual. Roll back route/model changes or disable exact counting if a model regression appears.

## Validation

- **At-PR unit:** allowed Claude list is tenant-scoped; non-Claude IDs do not appear in Desktop output; old generic list contract remains; count request retains tool schema and maps Bedrock inputTokens exactly.
- **At-PR integration:** fake CountTokens client covers success, unsupported model, access denied, throttle, and no cross-tenant model access.
- **Post-merge cloud:** from a clean cloud client, compare direct Bedrock CountTokens with gateway /v1/messages/count_tokens for identical model/body and verify Desktop-visible model IDs can be invoked.
- **Regression:** existing Claude Code and Codex model routing and gateway policy tests remain green.
title: Provide Claude Desktop model discovery and validated token counting

body:
## The problem in plain terms

ADP login already refreshes a token for Claude Code and Codex, but Claude Desktop asks for a separate Gateway URL and executable credential helper. Hand-entering a token expires, while an unpinned helper can later point at a different ADP deployment.

**The fix in one line:** Add a deployment-pinned Claude Desktop setup command that installs a refresh-safe helper and provides valid Desktop settings.

## Description

Make Claude Desktop onboarding a normal ADP CLI action after adp login. Reuse the existing token cache and refresh logic; do not create a second identity or store a static access token in Desktop settings. This child of #6850 follows the Bedrock proof and the selected gateway/model contract.

## Impact analysis

- **Who benefits:** laptop users who already run adp login and want Desktop on the same gateway.
- **Who's impacted:** ADP CLI installer/update bundle, local Desktop settings, support docs, and clean-room CLI evaluation.
- **Cost / quota footprint:** no AWS resources or inference cost from setup itself; an optional explicit connection test uses a bounded model call.

| Bug class | Blast radius |
|---|---|
| Helper uses ambient/default deployment | Desktop calls the wrong gateway after a deployment switch. |
| Token printed or persisted in config | Credential disclosure and expiry failures. |
| Setup overwrites Desktop settings | User loses unrelated app preferences/connectors. |
| GUI cannot invoke helper | Desktop sees 401 after a valid ADP login. |

## Design

Depends on story 1 and compatible model decision from story 4. Current main CLI lives in modules/gateway/cli/adp and already implements adp login, adp token, deployment-pinned Claude Code helper commands, and adp claude setup. Add adp claude-desktop setup as a separate verb; keep adp claude setup behavior intact.

Resolve the selected deployment, verify the ADP session, and install a small executable helper with an absolute CLI path plus pinned deployment arguments. The helper prints only the bare token to stdout, exits nonzero without a GUI prompt if refresh fails, and writes no credential to disk beyond the existing ADP token store. Restrict helper permissions. Determine the stable, documented Claude Desktop third-party-inference config/import format; if no supported writable format exists, print/copy exact Gateway provider, base URL, bearer auth scheme, helper path, and allowed model instructions rather than editing private app files. Make setup idempotent and preserve existing user settings. Add a no-secret status/check command or setup verification that tests helper exit status and gateway reachability without echoing the token.

Update modules/gateway/cli/install.sh, CLI bundle/download allowlist and setup documentation only as needed by the current main packaging contract. No DB or gateway auth changes.

## Deployment

CLI-only paths do not automatically trigger gateway-deploy.yml. Ensure the updated bundle is included in the gateway image/download route, and dispatch the dev gateway deployment workflow if packaging requires it; verify adp update retrieves the new version. No Terraform or agent image change. Production rollout follows existing CLI release/deployment process. Rollback via CLI bundle version/previous installer without removing the user's ADP login.

## Validation

- **At-PR unit:** setup twice yields the same helper/config; deployment switch does not change a pinned helper; stdout contains only token; helper failure contains no token; unrelated settings survive.
- **At-PR integration:** run existing CLI setup tests and clean-room eval dry-run suite in CI.
- **Post-merge cloud:** use a clean pod patterned on eval-cli-onboarding.yml, seed a dedicated test login, install CLI, run Desktop setup and helper, then issue one bounded authenticated /v1/models request; assert org/deployment identity and no token in logs. This verifies the helper contract without requiring a GUI in cloud.
- **Manual Desktop smoke:** on supported macOS/Windows app, import/apply the settings and run one basic chat; cloud protocol tests remain the release gate for tools.
title: Add deployment-pinned adp claude-desktop setup

body:
## The problem in plain terms

A unit test can show that ADP forwards tool fields, yet still miss a bad deployed model, expired login, streaming proxy, or usage attribution. Cloud agents need one repeatable test that proves the complete Desktop-shaped conversation without relying on someone's laptop.

**The fix in one line:** Add a clean cloud contract suite that runs a bounded two-turn Desktop tool exchange through the deployed gateway.

## Description

Build the epic acceptance harness and operator runbook for #6850. It must be runnable by cloud agents/ARC in dev and later target environments, use a real scoped gateway credential, and verify both client-visible tool behavior and ADP governance.

## Impact analysis

- **Who benefits:** cloud implementers, reviewers and operators; Desktop users get a release gate based on the real service.
- **Who's impacted:** live test workflow, temporary test pod, smoke identity, gateway usage records and Bedrock quota.
- **Cost / quota footprint:** bounded invocations with low max_tokens and concurrency one; no persistent test infrastructure. Daily scheduling only after observed cost and cleanup are acceptable.

| Bug class | Blast radius |
|---|---|
| Test pod inherits internal credentials | False green that bypasses the ADP login path. |
| Token/prompt exposed in workflow logs | Secret or test data leak. |
| Test asserts only HTTP 200 | Broken tools ship undetected. |
| Cleanup fails | Stale pods/identities and unnecessary cost. |

## Design

Depends on stories 1-5 and resolution of #790. Add platform/evals/claude-desktop-gateway/ with a deterministic client that calls the Anthropic-shaped gateway endpoints used by Desktop: /v1/models, /v1/messages/count_tokens when supported, and /v1/messages streamed and non-streamed. Add .github/workflows/eval-claude-desktop-gateway.yml with workflow_dispatch environment input and PR lint/unit-only mode. Reuse the clean-room split and contamination gate from .github/workflows/eval-cli-onboarding.yml: ARC holds control credentials, a short-lived pod acts as the Desktop-like client without ambient AWS/Claude/ADP auth, and an existing dedicated smoke-user refresh token supplies its scoped gateway credential without printing it.

The cloud client verifies: selected model is allowed; streamed tool_use has stable ID/name and reconstructable input JSON; it executes a harmless local deterministic tool; sends tool_result; final reply incorporates that result; non-stream equivalent works; CountTokens matches direct Bedrock or reports the documented unavailable mode; token refresh succeeds after expiring only the disposable test token cache; cross-org/disallowed model requests are denied; usage row/request ID is attributed to the smoke user and selected org. Compare sanitized event shape to direct Bedrock fixtures from story 1. A failure must name the broken layer, not merely return a generic timeout.

The workflow must assert target AWS account and region before any Bedrock or gateway call, cap model output/invocations, sanitize logs, and always clean up temporary resources. No new schema. The gateway remains the auth and accounting boundary; the client executes tools.

## Deployment

Test code and workflow merge with no service redeploy by themselves. Run the workflow manually after each gateway/CLI child deploys to dev using: gh workflow run eval-claude-desktop-gateway.yml -f environment=dev. Add a nightly only after the one-off run is stable and bounded. Production promotion requires a passing run against that target account and model. Rollback is disabling the workflow schedule or reverting the acceptance harness, not changing user credentials.

## Validation

- **At-PR:** dry-run the harness against fixtures with injected missing tool delta, wrong tool ID, 401 refresh failure, denied model, and cleanup failure; lint workflow/scripts; no live Bedrock on PR.
- **Post-merge cloud:** workflow passes against deployed dev gateway and records account, region, model, request IDs, event checklist and usage attribution in the run summary; no secret or prompt body appears in logs.
- **Regression:** Claude Code Bedrock pass-through, Codex route, existing gateway-live-tests.yml and eval-cli-onboarding.yml stay green.
- **Epic acceptance:** link the successful cloud run and documented manual Desktop smoke to #6850 before closing it.
title: Add cloud end-to-end Claude Desktop gateway test and runbook

body:
> **Parent**: #745 — Route agent-worker Bedrock calls through gateway
> **Discovered**: spike #765 retest #4 (2026-05-25). Non-blocking for spike closure but must fix before Phase 3 cutover.

## Description

The gateway's app-level translation between Anthropic Messages API format and Bedrock's `InvokeModel`/`Converse` format **strips the `tools` and `tool_choice` parameters** from the request body before forwarding to Bedrock.

Evidence from spike retest #4:
- Request body sent through proxy: 332-388 bytes (includes full tool definitions)
- Gateway receives the body intact (verified at network layer)
- Bedrock returns `input_tokens=14` for a request that should be ~100+ tokens with tool definitions
- Conclusion: tools array is parsed and dropped somewhere in the gateway's translation layer before SigV4 signing the Bedrock call

This is an **app-level bug**, not a routing/auth/network issue. The full chain from SDK → sigv4-proxy → API GW → VPC Link → ALB → gateway pod works correctly; the failure is inside gateway code.

## Why now

- Spike #765 closed with verdict GO for the auth/routing/streaming chain
- Phase 3 cutover (#748) cannot ship until tool-use parity with direct Bedrock is verified
- Agent workers depend heavily on tool-use (Bash, Read, Edit, etc.) — without tools, agents are useless
- Today the agents bypass the gateway and call Bedrock directly, masking this bug

## Impact analysis

**Who's blocked**: agent workers using tool-use (which is essentially all of them) cannot route through the gateway until this is fixed. EPIC #745 cutover is gated on this.

**Blast radius if shipped**: agents would silently lose tool-calling capability. Catastrophic — agents would either hallucinate or refuse to act.

**Mitigation**: kept on the direct-Bedrock path until fixed; gateway path is opt-in until validated.

## Design

The gateway proxy code lives in `modules/gateway/src/proxy/`. The translation layer between Anthropic Messages and Bedrock formats is the suspect. Investigation order:

1. **Find the request body parsing** in proxy — likely in `proxy/handlers.py` or `proxy/translators.py` or `proxy/messages.py`
2. **Verify**: log the parsed body before Bedrock call. If `tools` is missing, the translator drops it. If present, the issue is in the SigV4 signing or Bedrock client call.
3. **Fix**: include `tools` and `tool_choice` in the Bedrock request when present.
4. **Test**: send a request with a small `tools` array; assert Bedrock returns `tool_use` content blocks; assert `input_tokens` reflects the tool definitions.

### Reproduction (run from inside an agent-scaledjob pod after Phase 2-a applied + BG_TRUST_APIGW_HEADERS=true):

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9090/v1/messages \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -d '{
    "model":"global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1",
    "max_tokens":100,
    "tools":[{"name":"add","description":"Add two numbers","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"type":"number"},"b":{"type":"number"}},"required":["a","b"]}}],
    "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"what is 2+3? use the add tool"}]
  }'
```

Expected: response contains `content` with a `tool_use` block calling `add(a=2, b=3)`, `usage.input_tokens` ≥ 50.
Actual today: response is plain text or hallucinated math; `usage.input_tokens` = ~14 (tools missing).

## Files to investigate

- `modules/gateway/src/proxy/` — request handlers + translation layer
- `modules/gateway/src/api/messages.py` — if the messages endpoint is here
- `modules/gateway/src/proxy/bedrock_client.py` (or equivalent) — where the actual Bedrock call is made

## Validation

- Unit test: parse request body with `tools` array, assert it's preserved through translation
- Integration test: end-to-end request with tools, assert Bedrock returns `tool_use` block
- Smoke test: rerun the curl above; verify `tool_use` in response

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tools` array preserved end-to-end through the gateway translation layer
- [ ] `tool_choice` preserved (auto, any, specific tool name)
- [ ] Integration test asserts both
- [ ] Reproduces correctly via the curl reproduction above (returns `tool_use` block)
- [ ] EPIC #745 Phase 3 (#748) gate unblocked

## References

- EPIC #745 (parent)
- Spike #765 retest #4 (closed; reported the bug)

## Precision update — confirmed bug location (file paths in OP are stale)

Walked the gateway proxy code on `main` (commits up to 2379708). The "Files to investigate" list above is stale — the actual paths are different. Confirmed the bug is real with exact lines:

**Bug:** `tools` / `tool_choice` are never copied from the inbound request into the `BedrockInvokeRequest` body. The schema supports them (`modules/gateway/src/proxy/schemas.py:340-341`), but the two builder functions never set them.

**Two call sites that need the fix:**

1. `modules/gateway/src/proxy/format_translator.py:215-267` — `FormatTranslator.anthropic_to_bedrock()`. Builds `BedrockInvokeRequest` from `messages`, `system`, `max_tokens`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `stop_sequences` — but does **not** propagate `request.tools` or `request.tool_choice`. (`AnthropicMessagesRequest` schema has both at `schemas.py:236-237`.)

2. `modules/gateway/src/proxy/format_translator.py:69-142` — `FormatTranslator.openai_to_bedrock()`. Same omission for the OpenAI path. (`OpenAIChatCompletionRequest` has both at `schemas.py:84-85`.)

**Already correct (do not regress):**
- `bedrock_to_anthropic()` at `format_translator.py:269-315` already maps `tool_use` content blocks back.
- `bedrock_to_openai()` at `format_translator.py:144-209` already maps tool_use blocks → OpenAI `tool_calls`.
- `convert_bedrock_stream_chunk_to_anthropic()` at `format_translator.py:380-418` passes through `content_block_*` chunks, so `tool_use` streaming should work once the request side is fixed.

**Tests to add (alongside the fix):**
- `modules/gateway/tests/proxy/test_format_translator.py` — extend with cases asserting `tools` and `tool_choice` are preserved through `anthropic_to_bedrock` and `openai_to_bedrock` (auto / any / specific-tool variants).
- Minimum: 4 unit tests (anthropic+tools, anthropic+tools+tool_choice, openai+tools, openai+tools+tool_choice). Each builds a request, runs the translator, asserts the resulting `BedrockInvokeRequest.tools` and `.tool_choice` match.

**Reproduction in the OP is still valid** — the curl from inside an agent-scaledjob pod reproduces today against the deployed gateway.

**Routing fact (in case the agent goes hunting):** the request flow is sigv4-proxy → API Gateway `/agent/{proxy+}` → VPC Link → ALB → gateway pod (FastAPI). `BG_TRUST_APIGW_HEADERS=true` is durable in the configmap (PR #788). No routing changes needed for this fix.

## Audit Confirmation (from #806 / PR #807)

The gateway endpoint audit (merged in PR #807, doc at `modules/gateway/docs/endpoint-audit.md`) **confirms** this bug:

**Root cause**: `format_translator.py:anthropic_to_bedrock()` (lines 242-263) constructs `BedrockInvokeRequest` with only: `anthropic_version`, `max_tokens`, `messages`, `system`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `stop_sequences`. **Neither `tools` nor `tool_choice` are copied**, despite both being supported by the `BedrockInvokeRequest` schema (schemas.py:340-341).

**Affected endpoints**: `POST /v1/messages`, `POST /v1/chat/completions`
**NOT affected**: `POST /model/{id}/invoke`, `POST /bedrock/invoke` (pass-through paths that use `BedrockInvokeRequest(**body)` directly)

**Both auth modes affected equally** — the translation is auth-agnostic.

See full details: `modules/gateway/docs/endpoint-audit.md` § "POST /v1/messages (CRITICAL — tools dropped)"

## Runtime Confirmation of Tools-Stripping Bug

**Source**: Issue #824 runtime test (PR #829)

### Confirmed: `/v1/messages` and `/v1/chat/completions` DROP tools

Tested with `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` under both OAuth and IAM SigV4:

| Endpoint | Body with tools | input_tokens | tool_use in response? |
|----------|----------------|:------------:|:---------------------:|
| `/v1/messages` | tools + tool_choice auto | **19** | No |
| `/v1/messages` | tools + tool_choice forced | **14** | No |
| `/model/{id}/invoke` (same body) | tools + tool_choice auto | **578** | **Yes** |

The 19 vs 578 token delta proves the tool schema (serialized to ~560 tokens) is not reaching Bedrock via the translation path.

The model explicitly responds: *"I don't have any tools available to me in this conversation."*

### Root cause confirmed
`format_translator.py:anthropic_to_bedrock()` constructs `BedrockInvokeRequest` without copying `request.tools` or `request.tool_choice`. Same pattern in `openai_to_bedrock()`.

### No auth-mode divergence
OAuth and IAM SigV4 produce identical results — the bug is in the auth-agnostic translation layer.

Full results (24 test cases): `modules/gateway/docs/endpoint-audit.md` → "Runtime-Verified Proxy Endpoint Behavior" section.
